claim: *Dynamic context injection and enforcement.* A dispatch hook selects initial engineering knowledge from anticipated files and components. After planning, the agent selects context again using its refined scope. Standing instructions remain available throughout. A Git precommit gate requires evidence of the second selection for the initial commit that permits implementation to begin.
topology: Workflow: initial agent context → planning → refined agent context → Git precommit gate → implementation. A dispatch hook provides initial selection from anticipated files/components; planning sends a dashed refined-scope edge to the second selection, which uses refined files/dependencies and may add or remove context. Each selection feeds its corresponding context. The same engineering-knowledge repository feeds both selections. Standing instructions remain explicitly available throughout. No lifecycle return edge exists.
bw_encoding: Only the shared engineering-knowledge resource container has light 5% gray. Its standing-instructions and repository boxes remain white, as do workflow and selection nodes. Enforcement is distinguished by a diamond gate rather than a color. Row labels are bold 9.5 pt with italic 9 pt role annotations. Node titles are bold 9.5–10 pt, with Implementation bold 9 pt. Scope/phase qualifiers and inventories are italic. Body text remains 9 pt; no text is scaled down.
redesign: Author-requested three-row diagram separates agent workflow, dynamic context selection, and engineering knowledge as a resource. The top workflow retains initial context before planning and places the Git precommit admission gate before implementation. The author describes a bootstrap workflow: the gate requires evidence of refined selection for the initial commit that permits implementation to begin.
alt: Three rows distinguish agent workflow, dynamic context selection, and engineering knowledge as a resource. The workflow is initial agent context, planning to refine scope, refined agent context, a Git precommit gate, then implementation. The gate requires evidence of refined selection for the initial commit that permits implementation to begin. At task dispatch a hook selects initial knowledge from anticipated files and components. Planning passes refined scope to a second selection using refined files and dependencies; that selection may add or remove knowledge. Each selection feeds its corresponding agent context. Both draw from the same engineering knowledge repository of models, rules, procedures and examples. Standing instructions remain available throughout. Context retrieval supplies guidance; the distinct precommit gate enforces completion of the second selection.
